close_reason: Landed in 5805464 alongside JMAP-t307.2. The README How-to-use block now returns Result<Email, Box<dyn Error>> and uses ? instead of .expect(). The same rewrite covered the missed third surface that t307.2 named (README) along with t307.2's two surfaces (example, rustdoc) in one commit.
description:
Trigger: a consumer reading crate-jmap-mime/README.md as the starting point for their JMAP backend copies the 'How to use' code block at lines 67-94 verbatim into their `MailBackend::parse_email` implementation. The block contains `let msg = parse(raw).expect(\"parse failed\");` on line 68 — directly on the untrusted-input path (SMTP-delivered email bytes).

Consequence: every `.expect()` becomes a process panic in a server context. A single malformed message — truncated headers, broken multipart framing, oversized declared boundary, non-UTF-8 in a place mail-parser doesn't tolerate — kills the worker thread. SMTP delivery means the attacker is any party on the public internet that can reach the user's MX. This is a Section C 'parsing is total: no panic! reachable' supplement finding.

Relationship to existing bd:JMAP-t307.2: that finding names two surfaces with the same defect — `crate-jmap-mime/examples/parse_eml.rs` and `crate-jmap-mime/src/lib.rs:7-33` (the rustdoc example). Its 'Fix:' section says: '*Same fix applies to src/lib.rs:7-33 rustdoc.*' — it does NOT name the README's 'How to use' block. The README is in scope of this diff (newly-rewritten as part of bd:JMAP-76wm and the surrounding work) and is the **most-read** consumer-facing surface; closing t307.2 without updating the README would leave the worst version of the defect shipped.

Concrete site:

  crate-jmap-mime/README.md:67-94 (`## How to use`)
    line 68: `let msg = parse(raw).expect(\"parse failed\");`

Note this pattern pre-dates 9c0d34f — the README diff did not introduce it, it was already in the pre-diff README at the same line range. But the README rewrite preserved it verbatim, and the diff added `crate-jmap-mime/examples/parse_eml.rs` whose pattern mirrors the README's. The diff is the right moment to fix all three surfaces in one pass.

Fix: rewrite the README 'How to use' code block to:
- Change `fn parse_email(raw: &[u8]) -> jmap_mail_types::Email` to return `Result<jmap_mail_types::Email, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>`.
- Replace `parse(raw).expect(\"parse failed\")` with `parse(raw)?`.
- Add a one-sentence prose intro: 'A real backend MUST surface parse/decode errors as JMAP method errors per RFC 8620 §3.6.2, never panic.'

Confidentiality / integrity / availability classification: **availability**, exploitable by any SMTP sender to the affected mailbox. Same threat model as JMAP-t307.2 but on the third (and most read) doc surface.

Workspace tracking: crypto-security supplement to JMAP-t307; coordinate the fix with JMAP-t307.2's three-surface sweep.
title: README 'How to use' code block panics on malformed email: third copy-hazard surface missed by t307.2
